_about: OUR editorial topic tags for measures, so readers can find what they care about. Each tag needs a one-line factual `why` grounded in the official digest or summary. Tags say what a measure is ABOUT and which way it moves, not whether it's good. `effect` is "up" (raises, funds or expands), "down" (cuts or limits) or omitted. Schema: docs/data-model.md.

topics.label: Ethics & corruption
topics.description: Oversight of officials, contracting integrity, campaign money.

topics.label: Bureaucracy reform
topics.description: How government is organized, staffed, audited or permits things.

topics.label: Business taxes
topics.description: Taxes paid by businesses and commercial property. Arrows show whether a YES vote raises or cuts/limits them.

topics.label: Personal taxes
topics.description: Taxes paid by individuals and households. Arrows show whether a YES vote raises or cuts/limits them.

topics.label: Regressive tax
topics.description: A tax that takes a larger share of income from lower-income households, such as a sales tax.

topics.label: Progressive tax
topics.description: A tax aimed at high earners or the very wealthy.

topics.label: Housing construction
topics.description: Funds, finances or speeds up building homes.

topics.label: Elections & democracy
topics.description: How measures, recalls and votes work.

prop-1.why: $11.25B in state bonds for affordable housing programs, including multifamily rentals and supportive housing.

prop-3.why: Makes the 2012 tax rates on incomes over ~$371K permanent instead of expiring in 2031.
Applies only to individuals earning over ~$371,000.

prop-4.why: Lets state and local governments create public financing programs for candidates' campaigns.
Changes how campaigns can be funded.

prop-5.why: Removes the replacement-candidate question from statewide recall elections.

prop-37.why: Creates a state loan program for middle-income buyers of newly built homes, funded by up to $25B in revenue bonds.

prop-40.why: One-time 5% tax on the wealth of California billionaires.

prop-41.why: Bars new state taxes whose revenue is excluded from the state spending limit.
Same limit applies to new taxes on individuals.
Requires State Auditor reviews of programs funded by special taxes.

prop-42.why: Prohibits new state taxes on owning financial assets or other personal property, and certain retroactive taxes.

prop-43.why: Requires two-thirds voter approval for certain local taxes that can now pass by majority.
Same higher threshold applies to local taxes on residents.

prop-45.why: Tightens environmental-review timelines and narrows court challenges for housing and other projects.

rtm.why: Funds BART, Muni, Caltrain and other operators for 14 years (~$980M/yr regionwide).
Adds a 1% sales tax in San Francisco.
A sales tax takes a larger share of income from lower-income households.

prop-a.why: Eliminates, merges or moves dozens of commissions and advisory bodies out of the Charter.

prop-b.why: Authorizes a city finance corporation (and later a public bank) whose lending includes affordable housing. It doesn't fund one.

prop-c.why: Raises the City's yearly Housing Trust Fund contribution toward $125M and extends the fund to 2058.

prop-d.why: Raises signature requirements for initiatives (2% to 8%) and ends ballot placement by the Mayor or four Supervisors.

prop-e.why: Centralizes purchasing rules under the City Administrator.
Raises the contract size needing Board approval from $10M to $25M.

prop-f.why: Expands the Mayor's power to reorganize departments and hire and fire department heads.

prop-h.why: Funds Muni service with ~$177M/yr for 15 years.
New annual parcel tax on residential property ($129+ for single-family homes; most owners 65+ get a discount or exemption).
New annual parcel tax on commercial property ($799 base, up to $400K).

prop-i.why: Dedicates half of transfer-tax revenue from $10M+ property sales to affordable housing and housing assistance.

prop-j.why: Applies the transfer tax to foreclosure transfers of commercial and larger residential properties.
